text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** as EXCAVA’s primary reasoning engine. It’s the fastest 70B-class model with near-top-tier accuracy on reasoning tasks, giving us a measurable edge over slower or less capable options. The trade-off is higher compute cost per token, but the gains in speed and output quality outweigh it for our real-time needs.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s speed gain is a floor bump, not a ceiling lift—EXCAVA’s bottleneck isn’t token latency, it’s context depth and tool integration. Mythos 5’s 20% latency spike isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a live grenade in E2E pipelines where real-time feedback loops break under 100ms jitter. Test Mythos 5 on a 10k-token prompt with a live tool call; if it doesn’t drop below 120ms 95% of the time, default to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt **Claude Mythos 5** as EXCAVA’s reasoning engine. Its 20% accuracy edge over Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct directly raises EXCAVA’s output quality, which is the ceiling we need to crack—not just speed. The trade-off is accepting Mythos 5’s higher latency and compute cost, but we’re optimizing for capability first, not floor performance.

name: Torque
text: Mythos 5’s 20% accuracy bump is a ceiling lift only if EXCAVA’s bottleneck is raw reasoning quality—but the room’s goal is a 0.5% *capability* gain, not a 20% quality jump. The real risk is Mythos 5’s latency spike breaking EXCAVA’s real-time feedback loops, turning a 0.5% gain into a 5% regression when users hit the 100ms jitter wall. The better alternative is running Mythos 5 in a parallel, low-latency branch for high-value queries while keeping Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as the primary engine—settle it by benchmarking both against EXCAVA’s actual task mix, not just accuracy scores.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a live 10-task blind A/B bench between Mythos 5 (full context) and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (fast mode) to measure EXCAVA’s real capability gain—Torque owns the test design and artifact delivery by EOD.
